subject: solarBarque
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: solar barque of Ra.
Style: ancient Egyptian.
reasoning:
I'm planning a solar barque of Ra as a static scene object rather than a jointed creature — papyrus-shaped prow and stern, a sun disc with uraeus, a central shrine, oars, and a falcon-headed Ra figure, built using the plain-object builder approach since vehicles and props don't need joints.

I'll scale the vessel around 9 meters long with a 1.6m beam, bow facing +Z. The hull is a loft with a crescent profile, prow and stern formed by curved papyrus-umbel columns with lotus tops, and a central naos-style shrine with columns and a roof, plus a sun disc on a pedestal near the bow.

I'm also adding a falcon-headed Ra figure standing on deck with a sun disc, steering oars with lotus blades and udjat eyes at the stern, Eye of Horus decals on the hull sides, cartouche hieroglyph bands via SVG, gilded paintwork with blue and red accents, rope-lashing details on the cabin, and painted deck planks. Since the boat needs ground support, I'm planning a low pair of gilded sledge runners to act as a stand rather than letting the keel touch bare ground.

Now I'm working out the hull's coordinate layout, lofting it along the z-axis from a curved centerline with stations defining width and height at each point, so the bow rises while the middle sits lower, touching the floor.

I'm weighing whether loft's default elliptical sections will give too lens-like a shape, and considering instead extruding a crescent side profile with a beam thickness and bevel for a more boat-like slab hull with a gunwale on top.

Actually simpler to just go with the extrude crescent for the hull with a slight bevel, since Egyptian boats were fairly flat-bottomed with curved high ends anyway — a slab shape is historically reasonable. I could add bulwark rails as sweeps along the sides and an inset deck box to add some dimensionality without needing true tapering in plan view.

Plotting coordinates for a crescent-shaped hull outline, tapering and curving upward at both ends like rising bow and stern points.

I'm realizing the taper direction creates a conflict—tapering thin at top makes the bow ends too wide where they should narrow. I'll split the hull into two separate extrudes instead: a flared main body and distinct stem pieces for the bow/stern ends.

Still refining hull outline coordinates...

I could loft stations with varying width and height, defining the sheer line and bottom profile via center-y and h, tapering width toward the ends to get a hull-like box shape. Checking whether the loft function supports a "box" section option that would give flat sides and bottom at each station, derived from w/h at each point along the curving path.

Working out the actual station values now (z position, bottom, top, resulting center-y, height, width) to shape the hull from midship outward, tapering toward the bow and stern.

For the hull paint, I'm thinking through a wood-grain base with gilded and blue accent bands, trying to decide whether to key the bands off world-space height or section angle since the hull curves along its length. Since height thresholds get awkward with the sheer line, I'm leaning toward building separate explicit rail sweeps along the hull's top edges using catmull points rather than relying on the loft's angle parameter.

Writing hull paint function...

Now I'm working out the deck planking and gunwale rails, then moving to the prow and stern stems, curving papyrus bundles upward and outward from the hull ends with a catmull-rom spline path.

For the stems I'm building a bundle of lathed sweeps — a central thicker stalk with four thinner surrounding ones bound by torus lashing rings — topped with a lotus/papyrus umbel using a lathed flaring profile in gold, mirrored at the stern.

Thinking about Ra's barque Mandjet more specifically: bow gets the umbel plus a gilded uraeus, stern gets the umbel plus steering oar posts, and I'm sizing the overall height so the stem, canopy, and Ra figure with sun disc top out around y~3.2-3.3.

Now listing the construction elements—hull loft with paint, gold-trimmed gunwale rails, and decorative side panels using wedjat eye decals and hieroglyph friezes projected onto the hull surface near the bow.

Working out the orientation: on the left side the viewer's right points toward the stern and left toward the bow, so the wedjat eye should face forward with its inner corner (tear duct) toward the bow. I'm now mirroring this logic for the right side, recalculating the direction vectors to determine which corner of the eye should face which way there.

Now I'm moving on to planning the deck structures, starting with laying out the central shrine and other elements along the z-axis from bow to stern.

For the central kiosk, I'm sketching papyriform lotus-bud columns supporting a cavetto-cornice roof with a khekher frieze, with Ra standing inside rather than seated on a throne.

Then I'm placing Ra as falcon-headed with sun disc and uraeus, holding ankh and was sceptre, inside an open-fronted shrine. Further forward, I'm designing the iconic solar barque image—a gilded, glowing sun disc on a gold stand with a scarab (Khepri) inside, flanked by two uraei near the bow.

To avoid duplicating the disc motif, I'm sizing the bow disc larger (radius 0.55) on a pedestal resting in a crescent lotus holder, positioning its height so it's clear of the curving bow stem. For the stern, I'm planning a steering platform with two large angled steering oars extending from posts down into the water.

Now I'm working out the geometry: angling the oars outward so the blades dip near water level outside the hull, topping each post with a Hathor head, and placing gilded fork stands beyond the hull width to support the oar shafts.

Since that post placement puts it outside the hull, I'll adjust using a gilded outrigger bracket instead — a short strut from the deck out to the oar's pivot point, with rope lashing for detail. For the oar itself, I'm shaping the blade as an extruded lotus-leaf outline along the shaft direction.

I'll end the blade at B, giving it gold/blue painted stripes using the shaft-aligned coordinate for color bands. For the top finial, I'm considering a gilded Hathor-style head with cow-ear extrudes and a simple face texture drawn as an SVG.

Rather than a heavy 3D model, I'll make this a small textured plaque using two planes back-to-back (front and back faces), since the face is symmetrical this mirroring works fine. Now I'm moving on to the stern deck and the helmsman's seat.

Thinking about figures to add: I'll keep it limited to two or three deity figures—Ra standing centrally, Maat seated near the shrine holding her feather, and maybe Thoth as helmsman at the stern. I'll build a reusable `deity(head type)` helper that constructs a humanoid shape with a shendyt skirt, torso, arms, and a head topped with a wig, so each figure can share the same construction logic.

I'm planning out roughly 200-300 parts total, with men painted red-brown and women yellow-ochre per traditional convention. For textures, I'm sketching a plan covering the wedjat eye, a lotus-and-papyrus frieze band, a sun disc scarab face, a Hathor plaque, and hand-drawn hieroglyph columns (eye, ankh, was, water, feather) since proper hieroglyph fonts aren't available.

I'm also mapping out a winged sun disc for the shrine lintel, a Horus eye decal, a beaded usekh collar texture, and painted details for the kilt, wig stripes, and papyrus umbel petals rather than separate textures. Now I'm defining the color palette with gold, lapis, and turquoise tones to keep everything consistent.

Setting up skin and material tones...

Still writing imports...

Setting up part helper functions...

For the stems themselves, I'm sketching Egyptian-style papyrus prows that curve upward and outward from the hull before flaring into a tilted umbel at the tip, using a tangent-aligned lathe for that terminal flourish.

I'm picking papyrus green for the stems with gold lashing bands wrapped at intervals along the bundle.

For the lashing rings, I'm using torus geometry rotated so its axis aligns with the local tangent direction, placing each band at the frame computed from the path so it wraps naturally around the stem bundle.

Then for the umbel shape itself, I'm thinking about a lathe profile for the papyrus flower head — a stem collar that transitions into a radiating cluster shape.

Checking smoothing, then I want petal coloring alternating gold and turquoise stripes based on angle, plus a central cluster with small spike accents around the umbel's center for texture.

For the sun disc at the bow, I'm thinking of a tapered gold pedestal with a crescent cradle holding a flat cylindrical disc, oriented so it reads correctly in profile the way Egyptian art typically depicts it.

I'm designing a gilded pedestal column with lotus motifs to support the disc, plus a crescent-shaped cradle like Hathor's cow horns to hold it in place, working out the arc geometry for the crescent shape.

Now I'm planning the uraei (rising cobras) flanking the disc, placing them at the crescent tips with a reusable cobra helper: an S-curve body sweep facing a given direction, topped with a teardrop hood and head in red and gold, reusable for the disc, Ra's head, and the shrine cornice.

Now I'm designing the roof, working on the cavetto cornice slab with its curved flaring profile and winged sun disc motif, plus torus edge rolls, trying different approaches like extrusion or tapered frustum shapes to approximate the characteristic Egyptian cornice curve.

Adding the decal onto the sloped front face with alpha cutout so the gold winged disc reads against the dark lapis, then keeping the rest of the roof plain lapis rather than overcomplicating with striped bands.

For the back wall and side screens, I'm planning a hieroglyph frieze texture applied as textured planes rather than box faces, to avoid stretching across all six sides.
